thumbnail_diagnostic.why_this_slide: smallest round-1 slide (62 MB) whose tile-path FOV picks differed from the manifest
thumbnail_diagnostic.explanation: openslide's get_thumbnail reads the slide's own pyramid level 2 (downsample 16.004). GDC renders DeepZoom level 'downsample 16' from slide level 1 (openslide get_best_level_for_downsample(16) = 1 because 16 < 16.004) and LANCZOS-downsamples it, so the two thumbnails differ slightly; tissue fractions near the 0.75 cut can cross it, which changes the candidate list and therefore the seeded random picks. Full-resolution pixels are identical (equivalence MAD 0.0 on 23 crops).

tcga_labels_note: TCGA-BRCA provides no benign or in situ labels; only Invasive (primary tumor) and Normal (solid tissue normal) slide labels are tested.
limitations: Labels are slide-level sample types (Primary Tumor, Solid Tissue Normal); a tumor-slide crop may show only stroma or fat, and there are no tumor outlines.

TCGA-BRCA has no benign or in situ labels: four-class accuracy, in situ vs invasive and the p63/calponin rule are not tested; specificity is measured only against frozen normal tissue adjacent to tumor.
The reliability flag and the OOD percentile are not computed (CONCH and MUSK are not on this laptop); reliability_flag is forced false, which can only lower tiers relative to the app.
The sample is small (at most 25 patients); bootstrap intervals over patients are wide.

protocol25 crops come from the GDC DeepZoom tile API rather than local openslide decoding; re-extracting 23 openslide crops through the API reproduced them pixel for pixel, but the API's thumbnails can shift which tissue-rich fields are sampled (tile_equivalence).
BACH reference values are per image; TCGA values are per slide (maximum over up to 6 fields), so the BACH-vs-TCGA comparison is indicative, not a matched test.
Latency is measured on one laptop (Apple MPS) for single 2048 x 1536 fields, not whole slides.
Credit: TCGA Research Network (https://www.cancer.gov/tcga), via the NCI Genomic Data Commons.
